item.title: Decode One Instruction: sub rsp, 0x28
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64, MSVC-compiled binary, function prologue. Decode this raw byte sequence into its assembly instruction, and briefly explain what each part of the encoding means: 48 83 EC 28
Answer: sub rsp, 0x28
Byte breakdown: 48 is the REX.W prefix - the REX prefix byte (0100WRXB) extends the legacy x86 encoding for 64-bit mode; the W bit set to 1 forces the operation to use a 64-bit operand size (rsp instead of esp). 83 is the opcode for the Group 1 arithmetic instructions using a sign-extended 8-bit immediate; which arithmetic operation it performs is selected by the ModRM reg field, not the opcode alone. EC is the ModRM byte: mod=11 (register-direct), reg=101 (opcode extension /5, meaning SUB), rm=100 (RSP) - so this says 'SUB, operand is RSP itself.' 28 is the immediate operand, 0x28 (40 decimal), sign-extended to 64 bits and subtracted from RSP.
This is a classic MSVC function prologue: it reserves 0x28 bytes of stack space for locals and the shadow space required by the Windows x64 calling convention.
